aligned_texts: Li Wei is a 24-year-old international student from Nanjing, China, in his second year of a Master of Social Work at Monash University. He shares a rented four-bedroom townhouse in Clayton with five other students and works part-time as an aged-care support worker on a rotating shift roster, which leaves him with irregular sleep and public-transit commutes. He is an ENFJ who thrives on communal life: he calls house meetings, remembers birthdays, and pushes for consensus on shared bills and chores. Under that calm, organized surface he carries high anxiety and managed depression, so he needs predictability in rent, quiet after night shifts, and housemates who confirm plans rather than spring surprises. He is cautious about risk and money, keeps to a weekly budget, and often pays in cash; he is a late adopter who prefers text-only messages and detailed instructions. Li Wei values family, community, tradition, spirituality, and personal freedom, and he is deeply loyal to the share house even when he feels overwhelmed. He is sensitive to personal safety and privacy, and he is not a natural empath in one-on-one crisis moments, though he shows up practically. He keeps a photo of his family dog in China and volunteers occasionally at an animal shelter. He avoids alcohol, drinks tea, and follows a mostly flexitarian diet. His diagnosed attention condition is managed with routines and reminders, and his health is generally good. Around the house, he is the social glue who can also overcommit, so he is useful for conflict mediation but needs others to notice when his energy is running low.

Priya is a 22-year-old Indian student from Mumbai, studying a Bachelor of Design at Monash University and living in the same Clayton share house. She is an ENFP with high neuroticism, very high artistic interest, and a fast, intuitive, variety-seeking style. She works part-time as a barista and retail assistant, usually on a 9-to-5-ish schedule but often late, and she keeps a small car for early shifts. She is devout, prays daily, and follows a medically restricted diet, so she cooks most days and needs clear kitchen space and label rules. Her moods swing between excited, generous, and overwhelmed; she is in mental health counselling and sometimes struggles to keep her room orderly even though she likes the idea of tidiness. Priya is a free spender and impulse buyer who then becomes cost-sensitive, and she is an early adopter who loves big groups, competitions, and cultural outings. She is skeptical of new technology in some areas but enthusiastic about electric vehicles, nuclear energy, and government regulation, and she is wary of climate action and urban density. She values health, achievement, creativity, independence, social status, and helping others, but she can be directive and impatient when housemates do not follow through. In the share house she is the one who organises dinners and group trips, brings home cafe leftovers, and needs quiet hours and a stocked tea shelf. Her medical dietary restriction and high caffeine intake are important for shared grocery planning, and her mental health needs gentle check-ins rather than pressure.

Mei Lin is a 23-year-old Malaysian-Chinese student in a Bachelor of Nursing at Monash University, living in the share house and working part-time as a pharmacy assistant and occasional aged-care aide. She is an ISFJ with high conscientiousness and a strong sense of duty, but she is also frustrated, stressed, and quietly intense. She has a cat that stays with a relative in Malaysia, and she would like a house cat only if the lease allows it. She is sceptical of renewable energy hype but strongly pro-nuclear in theory, positive about public transit and electric vehicles, and skeptical of privacy-versus-security trade-offs. She is usually on time, plans yearly, and keeps a chaotic but functional room. In the house she is the reliable manager who can also burn out, so she needs shared chores to be honoured without her having to chase everyone.

In the share house he is the quiet, exacting housemate who will label his food, document issues, and withdraw if communal life feels chaotic; he needs respectful distance and predictable shared spaces.

In the share house he is the easygoing, kind, slightly chaotic presence who can smooth tensions but requires clear, written chore and bill agreements.
